LESSON: THE BUILT ENVIRONMENTS ● MUSEUMS ● MONUMENTS ● CULTURAL CENTRES ● HISTORICAL BUILDINGS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 1.5: The Built Environments ● Museums ● Monuments ● Cultural centres ● Historical buildings
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Built Environments ● Museums ● Monuments ● Cultural centres ● Historical buildings, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we conserve the historic built environment in Kenya?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Built Environments ● Museums ● Monuments ● Cultural centres ● Historical buildings together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Love: caring attitude as learners participate in conservation activities for historic built environments within the locality.

● Peace: tolerance as learners brainstorm the main historic built environments in Kenya (Museums, monuments, Cultural centers and

historical buildings).

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education: as learners visit a nearby historic built environment/library/cultural center and share experiences.

Link to other learning areas:

● Religious studies: as learners participate in conservation activities for historic built environments within the locality.

● English and Kenya Sign Language: presentation skills learnt in English as learners visit a nearby historic built

environment/library/cultural center and share experiences in class.

Suggested Learning Resources:

local and extended environment, print resources, digital resources, approved textbooks, maps of Kenya showing the main historic built
